app.title: Antibiotic resistance virtual lab: formula score, model prediction and observed rate for a bacterium-antibiotic pair
app.summary: A person picks one bacterium and one antibiotic from two dropdowns. The page shows a hand-built formula score and a trained model's prediction for that pair, and sets them beside the observed surveillance rate, or says no observed value exists. A donut chart splits the formula score into the share each resistance mechanism contributes, with percentages on hover. A separate report page explains how the two feature tables were combined, how both models were built and how they were validated.

task.text: Look up a predicted resistance rate for a chosen bacterium-antibiotic pair, check it against the observed rate and see which mechanisms drive it.

data.text: A precomputed cross-join of two feature tables: organisms by binary mechanism presence, and drugs by 0-1 vulnerability to each mechanism. Each pair carries per-mechanism contribution factors, a formula score, a model prediction and, for some pairs, an observed rate. A research report goes with it.
data.item: a bacterium-antibiotic pair with its mechanism factors, formula score, model prediction and observed resistance rate where one exists

stage.text: checking model predictions against surveillance data after modelling, and sharing the write-up

mechanism.text: Two dropdowns choose the pair. That choice filters the precomputed tables to one row, which fills a readout of the formula score, model prediction and observed value, and a donut chart of mechanism shares. The report page is a separate long document with tables and figures.

field.text: mechanism-based prediction of antimicrobial resistance with machine learning, in microbiology

workflow.name: look up a model's prediction for a chosen combination and check it against the observed value

steps.here: On page load, the precomputed supertable (mechanism factors and formula score per pair) and the predictions table (model prediction plus observed rate) are read from CSV.

steps.step: choose one combination of inputs to examine
steps.here: 'Choose a Bacteria?' and 'Choose an Antibiotic?' dropdowns list every organism and drug. The two choices filter both tables down to the one matching row.

steps.step: compare predicted values with the observed value
steps.here: The readout lists the formula-based prediction, the predictive model's prediction and the observed (real) value. When surveillance data does not cover the pair, it says 'No comparative data provided from ATLAS'.

steps.step: break a value down into the share each factor contributes
steps.here: A donut chart shows each mechanism's factor (presence × vulnerability weight) as a share of the pair's total vulnerability. Zero shares are dropped, and hovering a slice shows its percentage.

steps.step: read how the result was produced and validated
steps.here: The Report page sets out the method: a toy Table A × Table B cross-join, the scoring formula, gradient boosting with leave-one-out validation, and figures of predicted vs observed values and feature importance.

distinctive: Two models for the same pair are shown together: a hand-weighted formula and a regressor trained on observed rates, so a person can see how far each is from reality.
Observed rates exist for only part of the pairs, and the readout says so explicitly rather than leaving a gap.
The formula score breaks down into per-mechanism factors (binary presence × literature weight), and the chart shows these as shares.
Every number is precomputed by offline scripts. The interface only selects and displays, so nothing is recomputed or exported.
